The test image shows an opened soybean pod with seeds inside. Key features:
- White, cottony/fluffy mycelial growth along the inner pod walls
- Brown/tan discoloration on the pod exterior
- Seeds appear yellow-green but otherwise normal
- The white fluffy material is the most distinctive feature

This white cottony mycelium inside a pod is highly characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference shows White Mold causing bleached/wilted tissue. The test image shows the inside of a pod with white cottony mycelium — the classic sign of Sclerotinia (White Mold) inside pods. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of this disease.
